criteria.text: Treatment of acute abdominal, facial, or laryngeal HAE attacks in adults and adolescents.
Documented diagnosis of hereditary angioedema (HAE) by an immunologist (approval criterion 1).
History consistent with monthly abdominal or respiratory HAE attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months (approval criterion 2).
Patient is NOT concurrently taking an ACE inhibitor or estrogen replacement therapy (approval criterion 3).
Insufficient response or contraindication to BOTH 17α-alkylated androgens AND antifibrinolytic agents (approval criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Berinert Criteria Version 1; Last updated 1/7/2013; Approved 01/18/2013. The effective_date 2022-11-01 is retained from the archived stub and is not the PDF approval date.
Indicated for acute abdominal, facial, or laryngeal HAE attacks in adults and adolescents. The PDF supplies no numeric age cutoff; age eligibility requires manual review.
A letter of medical necessity and all necessary documentation substantiating every approval criterion are required; document verification remains manual review.
ER documentation is required to substantiate monthly abdominal or respiratory attacks requiring hospital ER intervention in the previous 6 months.

Both preventative medication classes must have an insufficient response or contraindication: 17α-alkylated androgens (danazol, stanozolol, oxandrolone, methyltestosterone) AND antifibrinolytic agents (aminocaproic acid, tranexamic acid). Any androgen contraindication must be documented by an endocrinologist; verify documentation manually.
The safety and efficacy of Berinert for prophylactic therapy have not been established. Prophylaxis is excluded by the closed indication.
PDL context: pdl_20260601_text.txt lists BERINERT (IV) as non-preferred (OFF) in HAE TREATMENTS, effective 6/1/2026.
Ekterly is an acute HAE treatment alternative requiring separate evaluation under its own criteria.
Firazyr is an adult acute HAE treatment alternative requiring separate evaluation under its own indication and criteria.
